edges.explanation: Both articles argue that successful adaptation to transformative technology (AI for PM; AI integration for business leaders) requires mastering domain-specific skills and practical implementation strategies rather than treating the technology as a universal solution, with both identifying common failure modes that arise from oversimplification.

Both articles argue that despite significant macroeconomic disruption from tariffs and geopolitical realignment, businesses and trade patterns demonstrate resilience and adaptation rather than collapse, with AI-related sectors emerging as growth engines offsetting traditional trade losses.

Both articles apply the same underlying logic of quality-over-quantity metrics to their respective domains: Article A argues that attention value depends on focus and intent rather than hours consumed, while Article B demonstrates that business confidence depends on company-specific factors rather than macroeconomic conditions, revealing a shared structural insight that aggregate measures (time spent, national sentiment) systematically misrepresent actual value and decision-making drivers.

Both articles argue that measuring aggregate consumption metrics (hours watched vs. tokens processed) masks the true value of engagement, which depends instead on quality of focus/intent (Article A) and precision of task-specific optimization (Article B)—applying the same critique of naive quantification to different domains.

Both articles apply the same underlying logic of structural mismatch—that raw quantitative metrics (consumption hours in media, trade volume in geopolitics) fail to predict economic value, which instead depends on quality factors (focus/intent in attention, geopolitical alignment in trade flows) that traditional measurement obscures.
